name: Work Permit and Resident Card (Employer-Sponsored)

requirements.blocker_text: Journal Officiel de la Republique du Mali: the employer must apply to the National Labor Directorate (Direction Nationale du Travail) for a work permit (permis de travail) before the foreign worker can legally begin employment -- exempt only for missions under 3 months with proper documentation. The permit is granted only if the position cannot be filled by a national worker ('le poste de travail a occuper ne peut, en aucun cas, etre pourvu par un travailleur national') and the worker holds the required professional qualifications. The employer submits a stamped request (200 FCFA), a motivated report, 4 copies of the employment contract, ID photos, and the worker's residence authorization; the Directorate decides within 15 days (1 month if further investigation is needed). No numerical quota on foreign workers is set. The permit's maximum validity is 2 years for a worker's first 2 years of residence in Mali, and renewal tracks the employment contract's own duration; renewal must be requested at least 1 month before expiry.
requirements.fix_path: Have the employer file the work-permit application with the National Labor Directorate, including the labor-market-test justification and employment contract, before the worker starts work.

evidence_required.document: Employer's motivated report justifying the hire

outcome.duration_length: up to 2 years initially, renewal tied to the employment contract's duration

sources.title: Journal Officiel de la Republique du Mali (hosted via ILO NATLEX) -- work-permit sequencing, labor-market test, fees, timelines, 2-year validity cap

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Mali). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- hard requirement sourced directly to Mali's own official gazette, tier 1 (accessed via ILO's NATLEX legal database, which mirrors the primary text rather than summarizing it). GENUINE STRUCTURAL FINDING, shared across this country's residence-based files (see ml_investor_residence.json, ml_family_reunification.json): Mali's foreigners' regime, per Decret 05-322 P-RM, does not appear to distinguish a temporary-residence tier from a separate permanent-residence tier the way many other countries in this dataset do -- there is one ongoing status, the carte de resident, renewed periodically, with no formal graduated pathway from temporary to permanent found in this build. leads_to_pr is accordingly set to false, not because Mali denies long-term settlement, but because this dataset found no distinct 'permanent residence' status layered on top of the resident card itself. citizenship_after_months (60) reflects the STANDALONE naturalization track's general 5-year residence threshold (see ml_citizenship_naturalisation.json), not a permit-specific automatic conversion -- residence accrued while holding this permit is expected to count toward it, but this was not independently confirmed. family_can_work left null: not addressed by the source reviewed.
